enforcement on industrial property rights for trademarks in e-commerce in Vietnam 
 
 
 

THE OVERVIEW OF RESEARCH SITUATION 
           AND THEORETICAL BASIS OF RESEARCH 
 
     In terms of theoretical aspect, the thesis clarifies the concept, content, and peculiarities of industrial 
property rights to r trademarks in e-commerce, as well as the concept and content of the issues of 
"establishing rights to trademarks in e-commerce"., "exploitation of trademarks in e-commerce", 
"protection of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce; Theoretical issues of the legal 
provisions on industrial property rights to  trademarks in e-commerce 
In terms of legal aspect, the thesis continues to analyze specifically the provisions of Vietnamese law 
on establishing rights, exploiting and protecting industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce, 
making comparisons to legal provisions of international law, other nations.  
About practical aspects: The thesis analyzes and evaluates the reality of enforcing the legal provisions 
on industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce in Vietnam, comparing with some international 
experiences and other countries. Basing on above, the thesis makes recommendations and suggest solutions 
to improve Vietnam's legal system and improve the efficiency of the legal provision enforcement on 
industrial property rights for trademarks in e-commerce. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER 1 
THEORETICAL ISSUES ABOUT INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY RIGHTS TO TRADEMARK 
IN E-COMMERCE AND LEGAL PROVISIONS ON  INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY RIGHTS TO 
TRADEMARKS IN E-COMMERCE 
    1.1.  Theoretical issues about industrial property rights to trademark in E-commerce 
    1.1.1. Concept, content about industrial property rights to tradmark 
    1.1.1.1. The concept  of trademarks and industrial property rights to trademark 
          The term “trademark 
From the commercial perspective: "A trademark is any sign that individualizes the goods of a given 
enterprise and distinguishes them from the goods of its competitors." However, depending on each country's 
peculiar conditions, legal provisions have been amened to suit its peculiar conditions as regard to trademark 
object (visible and invisible), entity (individual/organization/ legal entity) or distinctive function (high 
distinctiveness or low distinctiveness) 
The concept about industrial property rights to trademark  
From economic law perspective: industrial property rights to trademarks is a set of legal norms for 
regulating rights of organizations, individuals to trademarks and rights against unfair competition 
  1.1.1.2. Contents of industrial property rights to trademark 
Ownership Rights affords the owner 3 types of right: right to possession, right to use, right to disposition. 
However, with the characteristics of intangible asset, the contents of industrial property rights to this asset 
include two group rights: exclusive use right (it means that owner has the right to exclude others from using 
his or her trademarks during the time of protected trademark and rights to disposition for trademark. 
However, from commercial perspective of industrial property right to trademark, right to use means 
conducting acts relating to commerce for the purpose of generating profits when those acts are conducted ( 
generate profits). Therefore, within the scope of the thesis, the author analyzes the content of industrial 
property rights to trademark, including two groups of rights: exclusive right to exploit trademark, prevent 
others from exploiting trademark, rights to disposition for trademark 
        1.1.2. Concept, content, and peculiarities of industrial property rights to trademarks in e -
commerce 
        1.1.2.1. The concept of industrial property rights to trademark in e-commerce 
Industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce include the set of legal norms governing the 
rights of organizations and individuals to trademarks in e-commerce and the right to combat unfair 
competition related to trademarks in e-commerce. This includes the following groups of legal norms 
governing this issue: i) Legal norms governing the State's recognition of the rights of individuals and 
organizations to trademarks in e-commerce through the establishment of trademark rights in e-commerce, 
ii) legal norms governing the contents of industrial property rights to trademark in e-commerce and are 
determined by exclusive right to exploit trademark, the right to exclude others from using trademark  in e-
commerce, iii) Legal norms governing the protection of industrial property rights to trademark in e-
commerce iv) Legal norms governing rights against unfair competition related to trademark in e-commerce 

   1.1.2.2. The peculiarities of industrial property rights to trademark in e-commerce 
Firstly, as regard to the issue of establishing industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce: 
building up a mechanism to protect industrial property rights to trademarks in specific e-commerce is 
neccessary to tackle the problem of the co-existence of trademark rights in the real world and the virtual 
space, Internet. Regulations on objects used as trademarks in this particular environment should be 
narrowed or expanded or not, are there any peculiarities in terms of the regulation of signs used as 
trademarks in the e-commerce . Is the conduct of procedures for establishing rights the same or not the 
same as the procedures in the traditional environment? 
Secondly, regarding the exploitation of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce, 
peculiar problems arisen such as: Regarding trademark advertising in the e-commerce raised the issue  to 
what extent does the content of the trademark owner's rights extend in the e-commerce? How to resolve the 
issue of the acts of unfair competition practices related to trademarks and domain names in e-commerce 
requires a legal mechanism to resolve disputes between domain names and trademarks in the e-commerce. 
How is the principle of trademark rights exhaustion applied in the internet environment? Or determining 
the responsibility mechanism for e-commerce service providers, when third-party trademark infringements 
occur, also arises an issue that needs to be resolved in this environment. 
Third, the peculiar problem in protecting industrial property rights totrademarks in the e-commerce 
platform: stemming from the characteristics in the e-commerce platform, which makes it difficult to determine 
the aspects of the infringement of industrial property rights to the trademark such as: the infringing object, 
identification of the infringement acts in e-commerce, the location and place of the infringement of the property 
rights industrial for trademarks ; identify acts of infringement of industrial property rights to trademarks across 
borders…. This determination is the basis for determining the contents of jurisdiction to make judgements, apply 
the law, appropriate measures to handle acts of industrial property rights infringement with respect to trademarks 
in e-commerce. 
1.1.2.3. Basic content of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commercer 
  i) Establishing industrial property rights to trademarks in the e-commerce  
*The concept of  establishing industrial property rights to trademarks in the e-commerce  
Establishing industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce includes a collection of legal 
provisions defining signs, requirements must be met for a trademark to be eligible for trademark protection, 
protection mechanisms and procedures for establishing trademark rights. in order to legally recognize the 
owner's exclusive rights to trademark in e-commerce 
    * Basic contents on establishing industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
Regulations on signs used as trademarks: 
In e-commerce, what the peculiar problem should be raised when regulating signs to be used as 
trademarks in this environment? 
   - Requirments for trademark protection in e-commerce 

  In the e-commerce platform, will requirements must be met for a trademark to be eligible for trademark 
protection remain the same? Are there any peculiarity  or differences that need to be amended in terms of 
requirements must be met for a trademark to be eligible for trademark protection in the e-commerce ? 
- Mechanism of trademark protection in e-commerce 
Whether the peculiar principle of intellectual property about "territoriality" remains the same, or needs 
to be amended and supplemented when implementing in the e-commerce. 
- How to establish trademark rights in e-commerce 
   How is the issue of establishing trademark rights in the e-commerce platform posed, is it necessary to 
set up a separate mechanism for establishing rights for this environment? 
ii)Exploiting industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
* The concept of exploiting industrial property rights for trademarks in e-commerce 
It can be understood that exploitation of industrial property rights to  trademarks in e-commerce is the 
practice of organizations and individuals performing all acts affecting trademarks in e-commerce in order 
for the purpose of generating profits.  
Exploiting contents and forms of trademark exploitation in e-commerce: 
In the e-commerce platform with peculiar characteristics, commercial exploitation of trademarks in e-
commerce raises many problems related to the following aspects: 
- 
Exhaustion of rights to trademarks and parallel imports in e-commerce 
In the e-commerce platform, in order to operate  conveniently and easily, and avoid disputes, uniform 
application of the principle for exhaustion of rights in the wide range plays significant role. The principle 
for international exhaustion of rights need to be taken into account by policymakers not only in Vietnam 
but also international level.  
- 
The relationship between trademarks and domain names in e-commerce 
Disputes arise when there are users and operators of the Website with a domain name but not the owner 
of the domain name or a trademark similar to the domain name. So,whether the current territorially based 
system of registration of trademarks is sufficient for the emerging borderless electronic marketplace 
- 
Determining the responsibilities of online intermediary service providers in e-commerce                                           
It is necessary to define the responsibility mechanism of commercial intermediaries providers in the 
Internet and e-commerce platform. Determining that mechanism on the basis of principles, on the one hand, 
needs to comply with the model regulations of international law, on the other hand, it is also necessary to 
take into account the balance and benefits,  too heavy obligations should not be imposed to commercial 
intermediaries providers (ISPs). 
    iii) Protection of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
  * Concept: Protection of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce is the use of appropriate 
measures by the owner and the State according to the legal provisions  to prevent and handle acts of 
infringement on trademark ownership in e-commerce, and at the same time restoring the legitimate rights 
and interests of the trademark owner when infringed in the e-commerce  
Contents of protecting industrial property rights for trademarks in e-commerce: 

   -     Determining  infringement of rights in e-commerce 
Infringement of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce is understood as any act (action or 
inaction, intentionally or unintentionally) performed by a entity with civil act capacity, infringe (usually to 
the detriment of the owner) trademark rights in e-commerce 
- 
How to handle infringements in e-commerce 
The prevention of trademark infringements is accomplished through two groups of methods: i) self-
protection measures of the trademark owners themselves (self-defense measures); ii) through the actions of 
state agencies, owners can request state agencies to protect their rights through various measures: 
administrative measures, criminal measures,. Civil measures to control exports and imports goods related 
to intellectual property 
1.2. Theoretical issues of the legal provisions on industrial property rights to trademarks in e-
commerce 
1.2.1. The overview of the legal provisions on industrial property rights to trademarks in e-
commerce 
The legal provisions on industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce can be understood as a 
system of  rules of conduct promulgated or recognized by the state in order to regulate social relations 
arising in the course of  establishing rights, exploiting and protecting trademark rights in e-commerce 
arising in e-commerce activities 
Approach in governing legal provisions on industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
Because the study of industrial property rights for trademarks is interdisciplinary. Basically, the 
governing of the legal provisions on industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce is reflected in 
the  intellectual property law. 
Next, relevant intellectual property issues arising in the e-commerce platform, which are of the nature 
of e-commerce, will be governed by the law on e-commerce. In addition, it is the study of other relevant 
legal groups (Law on information technology; Law on protection of consumer rights ...) 
1.2.2. Structure of legal content on industrial property rights for trademarks in e-commerce 
The structure of legal content on industrial property rights to trademarks includes a set of closely related 
legal norms to regulate social relations in the establishment of rights, exploitation and protection of 
trademark rights in the e-commerce platform. It is possible to determine the legal content of industrial 
property rights for trademarks in e-commerce, including the following groups of legal regulations: 
i) Legal norms on establishing industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
ii) Legal norms on exploitation of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
iii) Legal norms on protection of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER 2 
THE REALITY OF LEGAL PROVISIONS AND LEGAL PROVISIONS ENFORCEMENT OF 
INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY RIGHTS TO TRADEMARKS IN E-COMMERCE IN VIETNAM 
 2.1. The reality of Vietnamese legal provisions of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-
commerce 
  2.1.1. Legal provisions on establishing industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
  2.1.1.1. Regulations on objects used as trademarks 
The concept of a trademark and the requirements to be used as a trademark is generally stated in Clause 
16, Article 4 and Article 72 of the Vietnam Intellectual Property Law 2005, amended and supplemented in 
2009, 2019 ( Law on Intellectual Property).Holographic signs are accepted for protection as trademarks, 
but the Intellectual Property    does not have specific legal provisions  for this type of trademarkmark. 
Intellectual Property Law in Vietnam has not yet stated the regulations for the use of sound trademarks as 
a sign used as trademarks 
2.1.1.2. Requirements must be met for a trademark to be eligible for trademark protection 
Requirements must be met for a trademark to be eligible for trademark protection 
Article 72 of Intellectual Property Law . In the e-commerce platform, it is  required that  regulations on the 
use of technical tools to support images in the e-commerce platform to be compitable with the development of 
e-commerce must be introduced , contributing to protecting the legal rights and interests of consumers when 
choosing trademarks of goods and services. 
2.1.1.3. The mechanism of trademark protection in e-commerce 
In the e-commerce platform, in principle there is no contradiction in the application of the principle of 
territoriality in the traditional environment or in the e-commerce platform. The peculiarities of the e-
commerce platform do not arise to amend the owner's trademark registration regulations. The protection 
mechanism based on trademark registration in the e-commerce platform is exactly the same as that provided 
in the traditional territorial environment. 
2.1.1.4. Mechanism for establishing trademark rights in e-commerce 
Determining the mechanism for establishing trademark rights in e-commerce is similar to determining 
the mechanism for establishing trademark rights in the traditional environment. Basically, the peculiar 
problem in the e-commerce platform related to the mechanism of establishing trademark rights is 
unnecessary. 
2.1.2. Regulations on exploitation of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
2.1.2.1. Using protected trademarks in e-commerce 
In the e-commerce platform, there are a number of issues that need to be governed by legal provisions, 
including: 
Firstly, using a protected trademark as an online marketing tool for the enterprise's products and 
services 
With this act of trademark exploitation, is it infringing the exclusive rights of the trademark owner? 
Second, using trademarks to create linkages in e-commerce 

The issue related to trademarks associated with e-commerce website linking activities is whether the use 
of trademarks in hyperlinks is within the exclusive scope of trademarks right? 
Third, Internet marketing and advertising activities have the emergence of third-party's trademarks: to 
what extent does the issue of extending the scope of content rights of trademark owners in e-commerce? 
2.1.2.2. The exhaustion of intellectual property right and parallel import 
Currently, Vietnamese legal system has not yet had introduced any direct guidance or case law about 
the exhaustion of intellectual property right and parallel import. Is there a uniform application of the 
regulations about international exhaustion of right and parallel import to  goods and services in this peculiar 
environment 
     2.1.2.3. The relationship between domain names and trademarks in e-commerce 
Regarding the determination of acts of unfair competition related to trademarks and domain names 
according to Vietnamese law: 
In the e-commerce, the Vietnamese legal system has not yet had introduced any specific guidelines on 
unfair competition acts between domain names and trademarks.  
Resolving disputes between domain names and trademarks in e-commerce: Vietnamsese legal system 
has not yet had introduced any clear dispute resolution policy about domain names and trademarks in e-
commerce. 
    2.1.2.4. The responsibilities of online intermediary providers in e-commerce 
The content of the responsibility of ISPs according to Vietnamese law needs to be further expanded to be 
compatible with the legal provisions of international law. 
2.1.3. Legal provisions on the protection of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
2.1.3.1.  Trademark infringement in e-commerce  
In the e-commerce, the problem of protecting industrial property rights for trademarks arises as follows  
i) trademark infringement acts in e-commerce take place more directly and commonly in traditional 
environment. ii) The possibility of trademark infringement in the e-commerce platform is higher and more 
complex than in the traditional environment, due to the coexistence of trademarks in the traditional 
environment and in the e-commerce platform. 
2.1.3.2. Legal provisions on measures to protect industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
Similar to other legal systems in the world, Vietnamese legal system has introduced legal provisions on 
measures to protect industrial property rights for trademarks, including: 
- Measures for self-protection of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
- Administrative handling measures on handling acts of industrial property rights infringement to 
trademarks in e-commerce 
- Civil and criminal measures for acts of industrial property rights infringement to trademarks in e-
commerce 
- Border enforcement measures for goods and services in e-commerce 
2.2. The reality of enforcing legal provisions of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-
commerce 

2.1.2.1. The reality of legal provisions enforcement activities of industrial property rights to trademarks 
in e-commerce 
The reality of activities for  establishiment industrial property rights activities to  trademarks in e-
commerce 
Although the National Office of Intellectual Property still accepts three-dimensional trademark 
protection. But, in reality, the National Office of Intellectual Property has not yet recorded any cases of 
three- dimensional trademarks of goods and services registered in the e-commerce.  
    2.2.1.2. The reality of activities exploition of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
In reality, the following acts need to be paid attention to when exploiting industrial property rights to 
trademarks in e-commerce: 
-Acts of using trademarks without the permission of the right holder on search engines, banners, 
advertising pages, websites 
- The resolution of disputes between domain names and trademarks in e-commerce 
- Determining the responsibilities of e-commerce trading floor owners 
- The intentional or unintentional act of the above acts has caused disputes over industrial property rights 
to trademarks,having certain effects on the interests of rights holders, which requires Vietnamese 
policymakers for legal system to have corresponding amendment and handling measures 
2.2.1.3. The reality of activies for protection of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce. 
Handling the problem of counterfeit goods and trademark infringing goods on e-commerce websites. It 
is difficult to identify many problems: verifying website addresses providing counterfeit trademark goods, 
evidence collection; identify the object of buying and selling counterfeit goods… 
The implementation of activities to protect industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce is 
carried out by the entities in accordance with the following measures: 
- Measures for self-protection of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
- Administrative handling measures  
- Criminal measures 
 - Border enforcement measures for goods and services in e-commerce 
Above measures are actively and proactively carried out by enitities . Therefore, there have been certain 
results. However, there are still significant challenges that need to be met. 
2.2.2. Inadequacies in legal provision enforcement on industrial property rights for trademarks 
in e-commerce today 
Firstly, in the State administration of intellectual property and industrial property for trademarks in e-
commerce. 
Secondly, the enforcement of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce is still inadequate. 
Thirdly, the current awareness of enterprises about industrial property rights to trademarks in e-
commerce is still low. 
Fourthly, consumers and society's awareness of respecting and protecting intellectual property rights 
and industrial property rights to trademarks in the e-commerce. 

Fifthly, the protection of legal rights and interests of consumers and the social community against acts 
of industrial property rights infringment to trademarks in e-commerce has not been thorough and effective. 
    Seventhly, some other inadequacies 
     2.2.3. The causes of inadequacies in the legal provisions enforcement on industrial property 
rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
Firstly, stemming from the causes in the state administration of e-commerce and intellectual property 
Secondly, the cause for the legal provision enforcement of industrial property law to trademarks in e-
commerce  
Thirdly, on propaganda, guidance and training on intellectual property, industrial property rights to 
trademarks in the e-commerce. 
Fourthly, as regard to consumer awareness in respecting and protecting intellectual property rights 
and industrial property rights to trademarks in the e-commerce. 
Fifthly, about protecting the legal rights and interests of consumers against acts of industrial property 
rights infringment to trademarks in e-commerce. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

CHAPTER 3 
COMPLETING LEGAL SYSTEM AND IMPROVING EFFICIENCY OF LEGAL 
PROVISIONS ENFORCEMENT ON INDUSTRIAL PROPERTY RIGHTS TO TRADEMARKS  
IN E-COMMERCE IN VIETNAM 
3.1. The requirements for improving the legal system on industrial property rights to trademarks 
in e-commerce. 
3.1.1. Ensuring  compliance with the Party's policies on developing a socialist-oriented market economy 
3.1.2. Ensuring the consistency, synchronization and feasibility of the legal provisions 
3.2.3. Ensuring the suitability with the conditions and level of economic growth of Vietnam 
3.1.4. Ensuring the harmony of interests of entitites 
3.1.5. Meeting  the requirements of international integration 
3.2. The solution to completing the legal provisions on industrial property rights to trademarks in e-
commerce in Vietnam 
3.2.1. Completing legal provisions on intellectual property rights 
3.2.1.1. Completing the legal provisions on objects used as trademarks 
The three-dimensional sign applied under the current Intellectual Property Law should be removed 
because it is not compitable for the digital space platform, unless a virtual space can be created in this 
platform. The regulation of signs as sound trademarks needs to be amended and supplemented in the 
intellectual property law in Vietnam. 
3.2.1.2. Amending the legal provisions of the Intellectual Property Law related to the exhausion of rights 
and parallel import of trademark protected goods in e-commerce 
The principle of exhausion of rights in the traditional environment is still applied in the e-commerce 
platform.  
Regulations on parallel imported goods in e-commerce, it is necessary to introduce exceptional case to 
the principle of exhaustion of industrial property rights to  trademarks in e-commerce. 
   3.2.1.3. Amending legal provisions of intellectual property law in resolving trademark conflicts of a 
“transnational” nature arising on the basis of trademark co-existence: There is a need for regulation to 
provide guidelines for  this issue, which should be supplemented with a provision on “an exception to the 
use of a trademark for the purpose of accurately describing the legitimate goods or services bearing the 
trademark”. 
      3.2.2. Completing legal provisions on e-commerce: 
It is necessary to develop an E-commerce Law to stipulate the rights and obligations of entities when 
participating in business activities in the e-commerce platform, and the responsibilities of state management 
agencies in e-commerce activities. 
The E-commerce law needs to develop a separate chapter to regulate the contents of intellectual property 
arising in the e-commerce platform, including amending the issues of intellectual property rights for 
trademarks in the e-commerce platform specifically: 

i) 
Regulations on acts of industrial property rights infringement to trademarks in e-commerce: 
Develop a concept and provide specific guidance on acts of industrial property rights 
infringement to  trademarks in e-commerce (developing a Decree guiding E-commerce Law 
enforcement including this content) 
ii) 
Regulations on counterfeit trademark goods in e-commerce: It is necessary to develop and 
clearly define in the Decree guiding the E-commerce law enforcement on how to identify 
counterfeit trademark goods and protect intellectual property rights. in e-commerce; order and 
procedures for collecting information to handle acts of intellectual property rights infringement 
in e-commerce; specific provisions on criminal handling for acts of forging trademarks in e-
commerce 
iii) 
Regulations on responsibilities of ISPs in e-commerce related to industrial property rights to 
trademarks: The Ministry of Information and Communication, the Ministry of Science and 
Technology need to coordinate in developing a Decree regulating the responsibilities of the 
trademarks. organizations and enterprises providing intermediary services in the protection of 
industrial property rights in e-commerce. 
iv) 
Regulations on inspection and supervision of exported and imported goods in e-commerce with 
industrial property rights protection claims for trademarks: The Government should soon issue 
a Decree on management of commercial activities cross-border e-commerce with detailed 
regulations on the rights and obligations of related entities… 
   3.2.3. Completing other relevant legal provisions 
   3.2.3.1. Completing the legal provisions on unfair competition acts related to trademarks and domain 
names in e-commerce 
Firstly, it is necessary to clearly stipulate in the Information Technology Law what is called the act of 
registration, possession and use of domain names with unfair competition for trademarks in e-commerce. 
Second, stipulating the content of "unfair" criteria in the registration, possession and use of domain names "with 
bad intentions" of individuals/organizations. Third, it is necessary to add provisions on trademark issues in 
Article 69 Protection of intellectual property rights in the field of information technology in the Law on 
Information Technology. Fourth, it is necessary to add the provisions in Article 12 on domain name registration 
in Decree No. 72/2013/ND-CP dated 15/07/2013. Fifth, in promulgating sanctions to handle acts of unfair 
competition related to domain names and trademarks 
3.2.3.2. Amending and supplementing the Law on Protection of Consumer Rights 
It is necessary to supplement in the Law on Protection of Consumer Rights the right to claim 
compensation for damage caused by consumers being deceived about information about product, goods 
and service marks in e-commerce; Articles on the type of company, legal entity, capable of suing to better 
protect the interests of consumers against infringing acts that cause damage to the interests of consumers. 
3.3. Improving the efficiency of the legal provision enforcement on industrial property rights to 
trademarks in e-commerce in Viet Nam 
3.3.1. Solutions for the operation of state management agencies: 

For the Government, the Government needs to build and complete the basis and policies for the 
application and development of the digital economy. 
For ministries and sectors (Ministry of Industry and Trade, Ministry of Public Security, General 
Department of Customs, Ministry of Science and Technology, Ministry of Finance, etc.), it is necessary to 
uniformly issue strategies and annual plans in coordination of actions to protect protection of intellectual 
property rights in e-commerce, including content on protection of industrial property rights for trademarks 
in the e-commerce. 
State management agencies specialized in e-commerce and consumer protection, such as the Department 
of E-commerce and Digital Technology and the Department of Competition and Protection of E-commerce 
interests (Ministry of Industry and Trade) need have an annual plan, coordinate in organizing training 
sessions on consumer protection in e-commerce, measures to identify counterfeit goods, goods infringing 
upon intellectual property rights, feedback process and provide information that infringes intellectual 
property rights. 
3.3.2. Solutions on the operation of  legal rights enforcement agencies 
For inspection agencies: it is necessary to complete inspection and examination activities on e-
commerce. At the local level, it is necessary to build a specialized department on e-commerce under the 
Departments of Industry and Trade. For industrial property assessors: To enhance the effectiveness of 
assessment activities, it is necessary to research and develop a framework of training programs and tests of 
industrial property assessment. For market management team, it is necessary to step up training and improve 
the level of fighting against counterfeit goods in the e-commerce platform. For the Department of 
Competition and Consumer Protection: It is necessary to put all resources into investing in facilities and 
developing  human resources for agencies and organizations to protect consumers' interests. . For the Court, 
it is very necessary to develop "Guidelines" on intellectual property for judges to resolve specific disputes 
in e-commerce, including disputes over industrial property rights over trademarks in e-commerce 
3.3.3. Solutions  for Trademark Owner’s Operations  
Firstly, enterprises need to register domain names, have knowledge, choose a dispute resolution mechanism, 
and fight against domain name misappropriation. 
Second, enterprises need to apply technological measures to manage and protect their trademark ownership 
in the e-commerce platform. 
3.3.4. Solutions for the operation of sales e-commerce website owners 
As an online intermediary, merchants and organizations providing an platform for e-commerce activities 
need to understand about intellectual property rights infringement  in general, industrial property rights for 
trademarks in particular, as well as taking useful measures and tools to contribute to building a culture of 
healthy competition and promoting the development of e-commerce. 
3.3.5. Solutions for consumer operations 
When participating in the e-commerce market, in order to optimize their benefits, and also to protect 
their own interests, consumers also need to equip themselves with basic knowledge, as relevant regulations 
to protect the interests of consum 

 
GENERAL CONCLUSION 
1. In Vietnam, in recent years, e-commerce has developed rapidly with e-commerce infrastructure and 
established legal corridor The thesis analyzes legal aspects of industrial property rights for trademarks in 
the e-commerce in establishing rights, exploiting and protecting industrial property rights for trademarks 
in this particular environment 
2. The borderless essence of the Internet has posed many challenges to the fundamental principles of 
intellectual property rights in establishing rights, exploiting and protecting industrial property rights for 
trademarks in e-commerce 
3. Analyzing the reality  legal system and legal provisions enforcement on industrial property rights 
to demarks in e-commerce in Vietnam, referring to international experience shows that Vietnam has made 
great efforts in regulate industrial property regulations for trademarks in e-commerce. However, recent 
adjustments have not fully solved the problems arising in the rapidly developing practice of e-commerce. 
4. Vietnam needs to complete legal provisions on intellectual property, on e-commerce and related 
legal regulations; improve the operational efficiency of law enforcement agencies in this field.

commerce, Journal of  Education and Society , No. 110 (171), May 2020

BỘ GIÁO DỤC VÀ ĐÀO TẠO 
           BỘ TƯ PHÁP 
 
TRƯỜNG ĐẠI HỌC LUẬT HÀ NỘI 
******* 
THÔNG TIN VỀ NHỮNG KẾT LUẬN MỚI CỦA LUẬN ÁN 
Đề tài luận án: Quyền sở hữu công nghiệp đối với nhãn hiệu trong 
 thương mại điện tử 
Chuyên ngành: Luật kinh tế                           
Mã ngành: 9 38 01 07              
Cơ sở đào tạo: Trường Đại học Luật Hà Nội 
TÓM TẮT NHỮNG KẾT LUẬN MỚI CỦA LUẬN ÁN 
Luận án là công trình nghiên cứu một cách toàn diện các vấn đề lý luận và 
pháp lý về quyền sở hữu công nghiệp (QSHCN) đối với nhãn hiệu (NH) trong thương 
mại điện tử (TMĐT), cũng như phân tích, đánh giá những quy định pháp luật, tình 
hình thực hiện pháp luật về QSHCN đối với NH trong TMĐT tại Việt Nam, so sánh 
với một số quốc gia trên thế giới. Trên cơ sở kế thừa kết quả của những công trình 
nghiên cứu đã thực hiện liên quan đến đề tài, Luận án có những đóng góp mới về 
phương diện khoa học như sau: 
Thứ nhất: Luận án đã phân tích một cách có hệ thống những vấn đề lý luận về 
QSHCN đối với NH trong TMĐT, cụ thể: 
- Làm rõ về mặt lý luận khái niệm, nội dung của QSHCN đối với NH; QSHCN 
đối với NH trong TMĐT. 
- Làm rõ những đặc thù của QSHCN đối với NH trong TMĐT. 
- Phân tích những vấn đề lý luận về pháp luật về QSHCN đối với NH trong 
TMĐT. 

Thứ hai: Luận án đã phân tích một cách sâu sắc và đánh giá toàn diện những 
quy định của pháp luật Việt Nam về QSHCN đối với NH trong TMĐT, so sánh với  
một số quy định của pháp luật quốc tế. Qua đó, luận án chỉ ra một số “khoảng trống” 
trong các quy định này. 
Thứ ba: Luận án đã phân tích, đánh giá về thực tiễn thực hiện pháp luật về 
QSHCN đối với NH trong TMĐT tại Việt Nam, chỉ ra những điểm còn bất cập, 
nguyên nhân của sự bất cập đó. 
Thứ tư: Trên cơ sở những “khoảng trống” trong quy định pháp luật, những 
“bất cập” trong thực tiễn thực hiện pháp luật về QSHCN đối với NH trong TMĐT 
tại Việt Nam, so sánh với các quốc gia trên thế giới, đánh giá mức độ tương thích, 
luận án đưa ra những yêu cầu, giải pháp hoàn thiện pháp luật về QSHCN đối với NH 
trong TMĐT và nâng cao hiệu quả thực hiện pháp luật về QSHCN đối với NH trong 
TMĐT.

MINISTRY OF EDUCATION AND TRANING 
MINISTRY OF JUSTICE 
 
HA NOI LAW UNIVERSITY 
 
 
              INFORMATION ON NEW CONCLUSIONS OF THE THESIS 
Dissertation topic: Industrial property rights to trademarks in e-commerce    
Major: Economic Law 
Code: 9.38.01.07 
Training institution: Hanoi Law University 
 
SUMMARIZING  NEW CONCLUSIONS OF THE THESIS 
The thesis is a comprehensive research work on theoretical and legal issues of industrial 
property rights (IP) to trademarks in Electronic commerce (e-commerce), as well as analysis and 
evaluation of legal provisions, the reality of enforcing the legal provisions of industrial property 
rights to trademarks in Vietnam, making comparisons with certain nations across the globe. On 
the basis of inheriting the results of previous researches related to the topic, the thesis has new 
contributions in terms of scientific aspects as follows: 
 Firstly, the thesis has systematically analyzed the theoretical issues of industrial property 
rights for trademarks in e-commerce, specifically: 
- Clarifying theoretical aspects including concepts and contents of industrial property 
rights to trademarks in e-commerce 
- Clarifying the peculiarities of industrial property rights to trademarks in e-
commerce 
- Analyzing theoretical issues as regard to legal aspects of industrial property rights 
to trademarks in e-commerce 
Secondly, the thesis has deeply analyzed and comprehensively evaluated the provisions of 
Vietnamese law, making comparisons to some provisions of international law. Thereby, the thesis 
identified  some "legal gaps" in these regulations. 
Thirdly, the thesis has analyzed, evaluated the reality of enforcing the legal provisions of 
industrial property rights to trademarks in Vietnam, poiting out the problems and its causes.  

2 
 
Fourthly, on the basis of “gaps” in the legal provisions, the identified problems in the reality 
of enforcing the legal provisions of industrial property rights to trademarks in Vietnam, making 
comparisons to other nations in the world, evaluating the compatibility level (compatibility rating). 
The thesis provides requirements and solutions to improve the legal system and the effectiveness 
of law enforcement of industrial property rights to trademarks in Vietnam.
